ledger_updates.subject: thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category
ledger_updates.affected_use:
Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

1.1 **Simples and standards.** By [F1], Levi-dominant integral highest weights are exactly the simple labels in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Their generalized standards are quotients of the ordinary Vermas with the same one-dimensional highest-weight space and simple head. They have finite length by [F2], and their weights, and hence highest weights of composition factors, lie in $\lambda-Q^+$ by [F3]. For any parabolic quotient of the ordinary Verma, the image of its highest vector is killed by the full positive nilpotent algebra. Its finite Levi span is the cyclic highest-weight simple $E(\lambda)$ by complete reducibility, and the radical kills that span since it kills the highest vector and is Levi-stable. The induction universal property therefore factors the quotient map through $\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$. This proves the largest-quotient assertion locally. This proves parts (1) and (2). [F1, F2, F3, F4]
